policy.purpose: Core (1A) is the difficulty-aware, prior-knowledge-aware subtopic-bucket teaching layer between source/Core (1) semantics and Core (2) transfer.
policy.primary_question_rule: Each Revised Core (2) v2 question belongs to exactly one primary SBA bucket; secondary prerequisites may be attached separately.
policy.production_selection_rule: For the current build queue, do not publish a dedicated SBA PDF when core2_primary_questions is empty; retain the bucket in the chapter map as SKIP_NO_PRIMARY_CORE2.
policy.priority_rule: Prioritise MEDIUM/HARD buckets for learners at or below 50% usable prior knowledge; increase visual staging, prerequisite rebuilding and worked-example guidance as readiness falls.
policy.core2_hint_preteach_rule: Every Core (2) H1/H2/H3 reveal must trace to an earlier Core (1A) learning atom and to an example/check; a question may be held until its release prerequisite buckets are complete.
policy.teaching_sequence_rule: Foundation/pretraining -> story/phenomenon -> staged picture -> what changed physically -> picture-to-maths bridge -> worked example -> guided/faded practice -> retrieval gate -> Core (2).

buckets.production_reason: Has one or more primary Revised Core (2) v2 questions; publish according to difficulty/readiness.

learning_atoms.title: Velocity is an arrow, not just a number
learning_atoms.purpose: Rebuild the instantaneous velocity vector from v_x and v_y and distinguish speed, velocity and component.
teaching_moves: show tangent velocity on the trajectory
split it into v_x and v_y
separate speed magnitude from signed components
misconceptions: speed and velocity are the same thing
checks: rebuild a velocity vector from two components

learning_atoms.title: Rising, apex, falling
learning_atoms.purpose: Track the vertical component through the full flight while horizontal velocity remains constant.
teaching_moves: hold v_x constant in every panel
keep g downward at every stage
misconceptions: the whole velocity is zero at the apex
acceleration becomes zero at the apex
checks: identify v_y sign and velocity direction at each stage

learning_atoms.title: Direction comes from the components
learning_atoms.purpose: Use tan(phi)=v_y/v_x to read the instantaneous direction and connect horizontal velocity to v_y=0.
teaching_moves: draw component triangle at one instant
teach sign of phi above/below horizontal
misconceptions: use launch angle theta as the later velocity angle

learning_atoms.title: Speed is the magnitude of the velocity vector
learning_atoms.purpose: Use v=sqrt(v_x^2+v_y^2), explain why speed is minimum at the apex, and connect apex speed to u cos(theta).
teaching_moves: show v_x constant while |v_y| shrinks then grows
misconceptions: maximum speed must occur at the apex
checks: compare speeds at launch, apex and same-height landing

learning_atoms.title: Same height: same speed, different velocity
learning_atoms.purpose: Use vertical symmetry to distinguish equal speed magnitude from opposite vertical direction at equal heights.
teaching_moves: mark equal-height points on rising/falling branches
misconceptions: same height means same velocity vector
checks: state which quantities match and which reverse sign

learning_atoms.title: When two velocity arrows must be perpendicular
learning_atoms.purpose: Teach a novice-friendly dot-product bridge and use v(t) dot u = 0 for perpendicular velocity events.
teaching_moves: introduce a_x b_x + a_y b_y=0 as the perpendicular test
solve the first equation before algebra
misconceptions: perpendicular means one component is zero
confuse the perpendicular event with the apex
checks: verify a dot product is zero

learning_atoms.title: Speed at a height without using the clock
learning_atoms.purpose: Combine v_y^2=u_y^2-2gy with v_x constant to compare speed at apex and other heights.
teaching_moves: compare squared speeds to avoid unnecessary square roots
misconceptions: use y measured from the wrong origin

hint_rungs.evidence: Perpendicular-velocity event is identified before equations.
Components and dot-product zero test are built visually.
Guided example starts with v(t) dot u = 0.
Apex/horizontal-velocity event taught on five-stage timeline.
v_y=u_y-gt and tan(phi)=v_y/v_x are connected.
Worked example calculates v_y first before direction.
Same perpendicular-velocity condition as Q01 taught.
Dot-product representation taught.
First mathematical move isolated in guided practice.
Minimum speed at apex and same-height launch/landing speed taught.
v_min=u_x and launch-speed triangle taught.
u^2=u_x^2+u_y^2 is used before range/height; full question released after SBA-05.
A later horizontal-velocity event is recognized as the apex.
v_y(t_apex)=0 and direction from components are explicit.
Two-time example works backward from the apex time.
At apex speed equals the horizontal component.
Apex speed ratio is translated to u cos(theta).
cos(theta) is isolated before the range formula; full question released after SBA-05.
Squared-speed comparison at apex and H/2 is taught.
At apex v^2=u_x^2 and at H/2 v_y^2=u_y^2/2 are derived.
